item.title: Peter Obi’s Bayelsa visit triggers political realignment as Ijaw leaders demand devt, unity
item.description: By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa The political landscape of Bayelsa State is undergoing a seismic shift following last week’s visit of Mr. Peter Obi, the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC’s presidential candidate, to the heart of the Ijaw Nation. This development, stakeholders said, has introduced a new dimension into the evolving political configuration of the state and the wider Niger Delta ahead of the 2027 general elections. Political analysts and Ijaw leaders who spoke to our correspondent described the developments as more than ceremonial, saying they signal the beginning of fresh political alignments and realignments that could reshape the state’s political architecture. However, he cautioned that “the success of any political platform must depend on its policies, credibility and commitment to the people’s welfare, not merely political structures or personalities.” Cultural Renaissance, Political Symbolism The traditional boat regatta at Toru-Orua, according to Okaba, underscored the importance of Ijaw cultural identity in political engagement. But he stressed that “celebrating our culture must go beyond ceremonial participation. Political leaders must demonstrate sustained commitment to the welfare, security and development of our riverine communities.” On Obi’s comments regarding federal attention to Bayelsa, Okaba said they “raise important questions about the marginalisation of oil-producing communities. item.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, November 5, 2026
item.description: The naira is trading at different rates against the US dollar across Nigeria’s official and parallel foreign exchange markets on Thursday, November 5, 2026. In the official Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM), the dollar is valued at approximately ₦1,347.30, based on the latest reported official rate. At the parallel market, Bureau De Change (BDC) operators are buying the dollar at approximately ₦1,380 and selling at ₦1,390. The figures indicate that Nigerians buying dollars through the parallel market are paying more than those accessing foreign exchange through the official window. The difference between the official rate and the parallel market selling rate is approximately ₦42.70 per dollar. Exchange rates fluctuate depending on dollar supply, demand, market liquidity and trading activities. The parallel market rate may also vary across locations and individual currency dealers. Nigerians seeking foreign exchange for international travel, school fees, business transactions and other payments are advised to confirm prevailing rates with their banks and licensed Bureau De Change operators before completing transactions. item.title: 2027: APC flags off Enugu campaign in Nsukka, vows to deliver Mbah, Tinubu, other candidates
item.description: …Governor highlights projects, promises more roads, jobs, infrastructure …Charges electorate to sweep away opposition with their votes The All Progressives Congress (APC) in Enugu State on Wednesday officially flagged off its campaign for the 2027 general elections, with party leaders and stakeholders pledging to mobilise voters across the state for the re-election of Governor Peter Mbah and President Bola Tinubu. The campaign flag-off, which held at Nsukka Township Stadium, witnessed a large turnout of party faithful, political office holders, traditional and community leaders, as well as supporters from across the three senatorial districts. Speakers at the event described the mammoth crowd as a demonstration of the APC’s political strength in Enugu State, insisting that the party was determined to consolidate its presence and secure victory for all its candidates in the forthcoming elections. Addressing the gathering, Governor Mbah highlighted his administration’s investments in security, infrastructure, education, healthcare, economic development, and revival of moribund assets and completion of abandoned projects. He urged the people to assess his government’s performance through its achievements and ongoing projects, noting that the opposition had not even presented any manifesto. Reflecting on his journey to Nsukka ahead of the rally, Mbah said the ongoing dualisation of the Penoks–T-Junction – Ugwogo-Opi-Nsukka road had significantly reduced travel time and improved safety. “I left the office a few minutes past 1pm. It took me two to three minutes to get to T-Junction from Penoks. And it just reminded me of how motorists could have spent so much time, sometimes up to 30 minutes or hours if we did not dualise that road. “From T-Junction all the way to Nsukka, I noticed that work was going on right left, green, what have you. The contractor assured me that a realistic commissioning date is before the end of this year. “Another thing the road reminds me is that we have kissed empty Mondays goodbye. Once upon a time, we dreaded traveling on that road because of fear of attack are gone. Today, we have kissed it goodbye,” he stated. According to him, the administration’s infrastructure programme is not merely about constructing roads, but also about reconnecting communities, expanding economic opportunities and promoting greater integration across the state. He cited the 40km Owo-Ubahu-Amankanu-Umualor-Ikem virgin dual carriageway, which connects to Obollo-Afor road as another intervention designed to improve connectivity, and now links communities in the northern part of the state, while also serving as a new gateway to the North Central part of the country. On education, Mbah said the Smart Green Schools initiative was fundamentally designed to transform the quality of learning and prepare children for a productive future and modern economy. item.title: APC has mechanism to manage our govs, Rainbow Coalition’s feud — Yilwatda
item.description: *We’ve no plan to make Nigeria one party state *Nigerians should choose leaders based on records, character, capacity to deliver *Says Tinubu’s reforms must translate into jobs, food, better incomes, security By Soni Daniel, Northern Regional Editor National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress, APC, Prof. Nentawe Goshwe Yilwatda, has said the ruling party has no ambition to turn Nigeria into a one-party state despite the influx of politicians from opposition parties into its fold. Yilwatda, who spoke on the 2027 general elections, governance and the APC’s preparations for the polls, said a strong ruling party and a competitive multiparty democracy could coexist. In an interview with Vanguard, the APC chairman also said the party had mechanisms to resolve differences between some APC governors and the Federal Capital Territory Minister, Nyesom Wike’s Rainbow Coalition, insisting that internal disagreements would not derail its preparations for the elections. He defended President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms, saying the administration had established measures to reposition the economy but must now translate them into jobs, affordable food, better incomes and improved security. Yilwatda urged Nigerians to assess candidates on their records, character and capacity to deliver rather than allow political differences to dictate their choices. As a democrat, are you not worried that the mass exodus of other politicians into the ruling APC can create a one-party state if the APC wins in January next year? I am a democrat, and I believe that Nigeria’s democracy is stronger when political parties are vibrant, competitive and able to offer citizens credible alternatives. The APC does not seek to eliminate opposition, nor do we believe that a healthy democracy can be sustained without it. The movement of politicians from one party to another is a feature of democratic politics. Individuals make such decisions for different reasons, and every Nigerian has the constitutional right to freedom of association. What matters is that these movements are voluntary and conducted in accordance with the law. However, the responsibility for maintaining a competitive political environment does not rest with the APC alone. Opposition parties must also strengthen their internal structures, build public confidence, articulate credible policies and organise effectively. Our ambition is not to turn Nigeria into a one-party state. Our ambition is to build a party that Nigerians freely choose because of its leadership, programmes and record of performance. A strong APC and a competitive multiparty democracy are not mutually exclusive. We will continue to respect the rights of other parties to organise, campaign and seek the people’s mandate. How is the APC under your leadership helping to actualise the dream of progressive politics, which seeks to make life better for all and reduce authoritarianism? item.title: ‘How BVN exposed fake Amnesty beneficiaries’
item.description: By John Alechenu ABUJA—The Presidential Amnesty Programme, PAP, has said its insistence on the Federal Government’s Bank Verification Number, BVN, policy has exposed fake beneficiaries and fraudsters feeding off the programme. The office, while condemning what it described as blackmail and campaign of calumny against its administrator, Dr. Dennis Otuaro, by some misguided elements from the Niger Delta, said it would not succumb to blackmail and will not sideline the BVN policy designed to link all bank accounts belonging to individuals and eradicate corruption. “The PAP office cannot be the exception in the execution of the government’s policy on BVN designed to eradicate corruption in the society,” the Office said in a statement, yesterday, Mr. Igoniko Oduma, Special Assistant on Media to the Administrator, said. “Clearly, anybody using the tool of blackmail to arm-twist the office to sideline BVN is either a criminal or a fraudster, who should be under security watch. The Office has asked them to come for verification of their claims, but they will not. “These serial blackmailers are purveyors of falsehood and hollow narratives; they are driven by sheer greed with the sole objective of denting Dr. Otuaro’s image and distracting him from focusing on the task given to him by President Bola Tinubu. “These misguided elements are angry with Dr. Otuaro for prudent management of resources, and introducing reforms that have sanitised the PAP. Many of them are angered by what is statutorily paid to them by the Office. Some want to be awarded bogus contracts which, the office under Otuaro, is not inclined to do.” The programme said rather than divert funds to satisfy blackmailers, resources are being deployed efficiently for lasting peace and security in the Niger Delta, with tangible results including 13,300 onshore and over 500 offshore scholarships, distribution of laptops to beneficiaries, and prompt payment of ex-agitators’ monthly stipends. It listed other achievements as employment of four cadet pilots and 20 aviation trainees after training, on-the-job training for 40 cadets, professional certification for 98 maritime cadets, and training of over 360 stakeholders on alternative dispute resolution and mediation. item.title: State Police: Kano, Cross River, Abia, Niger, Benue, Oyo yet to approve bill; gets Nov 19 deadline
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA—THERE are strong indications that the National Assembly is prepared to transmit the State Police Bill to President Bola Tinubu for assent as thirty states have so far approved the bill. The proposed State Police system has crossed a major constitutional hurdle, with 30 State Houses of Assembly approving the amendment required to pave the way for its establishment. This leaves six states yet to submit approved bill to the National Assembly for onward transmission to the President for subsequent assent. The six states that have not approved the bill are Kano, Cross River, Abia, Niger, Benue and Oyo. The Senate has, however, given them up till November 15 to do so, warning that failure to respond by the deadline could be deemed as withholding approval. The six states are expected to communicate their decisions before November 15, when the National Assembly intends to forward the proposed constitutional amendment to President Bola Tinubu for subsequent. Disclosing these while updating lawmakers on the progress of consultations with the 36 state legislatures on the proposed amendment yesterday, the Senate Leader, Senator Opeyemi Bamidele, APC, Ekiti Central, said the number of approvals had exceeded the constitutionally required two-thirds of the 36 state legislatures. According to him, for the process to be rounded off, it has to be in three phases, with the National Assembly expected to pass the bill; the approval by at least two-thirds of the state legislature; and the President to sign the bill into law. He added that the National Assembly had fulfilled its responsibility by passing the bill and transmitting it to all 36 State Houses of Assembly for consideration and approval. Bamidele said: “Let me explain again, for the avoidance of doubt, three keywords are used in the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999, as amended. The first word is passage, the second word is approval and the third assent. “The reason the writers of our Constitution, our forefathers, put all these specific words is to ensure that no part of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria can be easily amended without the buying in of all the critical stakeholders at all levels of governance. “The passage of the bill was the responsibility of the National Assembly, and that has been completed. Approval is required from at least two-thirds of the 36 State Houses of Assembly in the country, while assent must subsequently be given by the President to complete the constitutional amendment process.’’ He explained that the constitutional requirements were deliberately designed to ensure that amendments to the nation’s supreme law enjoyed the participation and agreement of critical stakeholders across the different levels of government. item.title: Voter register: INEC to purge 1.5m irregular registrants
item.description: •Amupitan can’t supervise credible polls in 2027 — Ezekwesili By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA—The Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, is set to delete about 1.5 million voter registrations found to be irregular from the national register, ahead of the 2027 general elections. This is even as former Education Minister, Oby Ezekwesili, said yesterday that Nigeria could not conduct a credible 2027 election under an Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, led by Prof. Joash Amupitan. INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan SAN, disclosed this while receiving a delegation on a courtesy visit to the commission’s headquarters in Abuja yesterday. The delegation was led by the Special Representative of the United Nations Secretary-General for West Africa and the Sahel and Head of the United Nations Office for West Africa and the Sahel, UNOWAS, Mr. Leonardo Santos Simão. Amupitan said technology-enabled verification helped the commission isolate the affected entries. The deletions, he explained, were part of a comprehensive cleaning of the register through the claims and objections process. The final register is scheduled for publication on December 15, 2026. Amupitan said the commission had registered approximately 103 million voters, with young Nigerians, aged 18 to 34, making up nearly 29 per cent of them. Amupitan said INEC would continue to strengthen the use of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System, BVAS, for accreditation, and the INEC Result Viewing Portal, IreV, for public access to polling-unit results. He said the commission was also planning a mock accreditation and election to test these tools, identify possible challenges and build public confidence before the 2027 polls. Amupitan identified misinformation, disinformation and foreign information manipulation as major threats to electoral integrity. He warned that the growing misuse of Artificial Intelligence, AI, and coordinated online campaigns could undermine public confidence in the electoral system. INEC under Amupitan can’t supervise credible polls in 2027, says Ezekwesili Meanwhile, former Education Minister, Oby Ezekwesili, has said Nigeria cannot conduct a credible 2027 election under an Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, led by Prof. Joash Amupitan. According to her, INEC has lost all credibility to be an independent umpire of Nigeria’s elections. Oby, who spoke against the backdrop of allegations of corruption involving the voter register through the use of artificial intelligence, noted that INEC’s Director of Information and Communication Technology, Dr Lawrence Bayode, on October 30, 2026, told Nigerians that INEC registration officers purportedly used their official login credentials to inject AI-generated photographs, duplicate records and other fabricated entries into the preliminary register of voters. item.title: Flamingos beat Brazil to reach first U17 Women World Cup final
item.description: Nigeria’s U17 women’s team, the Flamingos, have reached the final of the FIFA U17 Women’s World Cup for the first time in history after defeating Brazil 3-1 in the semi-final. The Flamingos secured the historic victory with goals from Queen Joseph and Awawu Bashiru, who scored twice. Joseph opened the scoring in the 56th minute before Bashiru extended Nigeria’s lead in the 71st minute. Bashiru completed her brace in the 80th minute to seal Nigeria’s 3-1 victory and book their place in the final. The achievement marks a major milestone for the Nigerian side, who won bronze at the 2022 edition of the competition. The Flamingos will now face Japan in the final as they seek to win their first-ever FIFA U17 Women’s World Cup title. item.title: FG records N4.69trn fiscal deficit in Q1’26 as revenue falls
item.description: •Nigeria’s economy grows 3.89% – Budget Office By Udeme Akpan The Federal Government (FG) recorded an aggregate fiscal deficit of N4.69 trillion in the first quarter of 2026, as revenue generation fell significantly below target, highlighting challenges in financing the 2026 budget. This came as Nigeria’s economy grew by 3.89 per cent in real terms during the quarter, driven by improved performance in the oil and non-oil sectors. Figures from the Budget Office of the Federation (BOF), contained in its 2026 Budget Performance Report, showed that the fiscal deficit was N4.69 trillion, compared with the prorated target of N7.86 trillion for the January–March period, representing N3.18 trillion below projection. The report showed that aggregate Federal Government revenue stood at N5.08 trillion, compared with the quarterly target of N9.22 trillion, resulting in a shortfall of N4.14 trillion. This represented about 55 per cent of projected revenue. Similarly, aggregate government expenditure amounted to N9.76 trillion, against the projected N17.08 trillion, indicating an underperformance of N7.32 trillion, or about 57.2 per cent of the target. On deficit financing, domestic borrowing stood at N3.9 trillion, compared with the prorated target of N4.61 trillion, leaving a shortfall of N704.03 billion. However, foreign borrowing, projected at N2.70 trillion for the quarter, recorded no actual inflow during the period. The Federal Government also realised N287.44 billion from multilateral and bilateral project-tied loans, against the quarterly target of N512.23 billion, while privatisation proceeds stood at N3.32 billion, compared with the projected N47.29 billion. The figures highlight the government’s difficulties in generating sufficient revenue and accessing planned financing sources to support budget implementation. Nigeria’s economy grows 3.89% On economic performance, the Budget Office reported that the oil sector grew by 2.57 per cent year-on-year in real terms during the first quarter, up by 0.70 percentage points from 1.87 per cent recorded in the corresponding period of 2025. The non-oil sector expanded by 3.94 per cent, outperforming the oil sector and accounting for a larger share of the economy’s growth. The Budget Office described the performance as “a period of macroeconomic stabilisation accompanied by moderate real-sector expansion.” However, it identified weak, although improving, revenue performance as a major constraint to budget execution, noting that the Federal Government continued to meet its non-discretionary expenditure obligations. It stated: “Improving revenue collections in the subsequent quarters of the year is critical to the successful execution of the 2026 Budget.” The report said the government would intensify efforts to improve economic growth and revenue generation, while controlling recurrent expenditure, particularly personnel costs. item.title: Police arrest suspect over attack on Obi’s convoy in Calabar
item.description: By Ike Uchechukwu, CALABAR The Cross River State Police Command on Wednesday arrested a 27-year-old man, Victor Edet Yellow Duke, in connection with an attack on the convoy of the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Mr Peter Obi, in Calabar, the state capital. The attack left the windshields of some vehicles smashed. The incident occurred at about 2:20 p.m. at the Watt Market Roundabout as the convoy was returning from the palace of the Obong of Calabar to Metropolitan Hotel, the venue of the party’s presidential town hall meeting. According to the police, a group of suspected hoodlums, reportedly armed with machetes and sticks, emerged from the Calabar Road and Clerks Alley axis and attacked vehicles in the convoy. The number of vehicles affected had not been ascertained. Police personnel deployed in the area moved in swiftly to contain the situation. Their intervention, which included the use of tear gas, led to the arrest of the suspect, while the other attackers fled. The suspect was later taken to the State Police Headquarters by operatives of the Violent Crime Response Unit, VCRU, for what the command described as a discreet investigation, to prevent reprisals or a further breakdown of law and order. Normalcy has since returned to the area. In a statement by its Police Public Relations Officer, ASP Sunday Eitokpah, the command said the Commissioner of Police, CP Ajo Geoffrey Ordue, had ordered a thorough investigation to identify and arrest other participants and establish the full circumstances of the incident. Cautioning against presuming the suspect’s guilt, the police said: “The arrest of a suspect does not amount to a determination of guilt, as the suspect remains entitled to the presumption of innocence pending the conclusion of investigation and any subsequent judicial proceedings.” The command assured residents, political stakeholders and visitors that adequate security measures remained in place across the state. It reiterated its commitment to “providing equal security protection to all political parties, candidates and their supporters, irrespective of political affiliation.” It also urged the public to stay calm, avoid spreading unverified information and report suspicious activities through established police channels. Eitokpah added: “The Cross River State Police Command remains committed to maintaining public safety, protecting democratic participation and ensuring that all lawful political activities are conducted in a peaceful and secure environment.” The post Police arrest suspect over attack on Obi’s convoy in Calabar appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: US Midterms: Implications of democrats’ victory
item.description: PRESIDENT Donald Trump has acknowledged the impact of the United States’ attack on Iran and a sharp rise in gasoline prices on stunning Republican losses in midterm elections, but said the move was justified and denied responsibility for the rout. The Democrats won both the US Senate and House of Representatives, taking control of Congress for the rest of Donald Trump’s presidency. The tally showed that Democrats grabbed 54 and 234 seats at press time to win the Senate and House of Representatives respectively. Historic firsts The election also delivered some historic firsts with the Democrats flipping at least seven Senate seats in ruby-red states and battlegrounds like Kansas, which hasn’t elected a Democratic senator in nearly a century, Iowa, Texas, Ohio, Maine, North Carolina and South Carolina. They held on to battleground seats in Georgia and Michigan. In the the House, Democrats would start the year with what would be its largest majority in nearly two decades, NBC News projects. Democrats flipped more than two dozen districts, some that voted for Trump by double digits in 2024. In the gubernatorial races, Democrats also flipped GOP-held offices: Keisha Lance Bottoms in Georgia, Amy Acton in Ohio, Rob Sand in Iowa, Gina Hinojosa in Texas and Aaron Ford in Nevada. Specifically, David Crowley, Democrat, has become the first Black governor in U.S history, Abdul El-Sayed becomes the first Muslim ever elected to the U.S. Senate, James Talarico becomes the first Democrat elected in Texas since 1988, Xavier Becerra becomes the first Latino elected governor in California history, Gina Hinojosa becomes the first Latina elected governor in Texas history, while Deb Haaland becomes the first Native American woman elected governor in U.S. History. I’m willing to accept results, work with Democrats – Trump Reacting to the election defeat, Trump said he was willing to accept the results of the midterm elections and work with Democrats as they made gains across the country. “We’ll, you know, look forward to working with them,” he told The New York Times shortly before 10:30 p.m. while watching results come in. “We’ll probably work something out.” Trump said Democrats had reached out to him about working together and that he thought they could find common ground on the debt ceiling. He added that he has “total veto power, so they have to come to us.” In a preview of his likely governing style over the next two years, Trump also posted a picture of his trademark red cap emblazoned with the word “veto” to convey his determination to block legislation carried by the incoming Democratic-controlled Congress. item.title: Atiku breaks through in Sokoto
item.description: By Abubakar Auwal, Salim Ashir Mahuta, Sokoto & Mumini Abdulkareem, Ilorin The African Democratic Congress (ADC) finally held its presidential campaign flag-off in Sokoto on Wednesday after uncertainty over the venue of the rally and whether the party would be allowed to hold the event in the state. The event was largely peaceful, but some party supporters were alleged to have come under attack en route to the campaign ground, with two persons reportedly shot. Analysts say the flag-off represents a breakthrough for the opposition, as the atmosphere had been dominated by the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), which began its campaign on October 24, in Kaduna. The ADC campaign flag-off was held against the backdrop of hostility the party faced preparatory to the event, including the takeover of hotel accommodation allegedly by the state government, the sealing of its party secretariat and refusal to grant the use of public squares for the event. Even as at late Tuesday night, few hours to the D-Day, it wasn’t clear if the rally was going to take place as the presidential candidate of the party, Alhaji Atiku Abubakar and his running mate, Rotimi Amaechi; the national chairman of the party, Senator David Mark and other members of the party were yet to arrive at the state. By early Wednesday morning, things began to shape up when the party scaled over a major hurdle and secured a venue for the rally. The ADC announced on Wednesday, that its state secretariat along Ilorin Road, Sokoto, would serve as the venue for the presidential campaign flag-off. It was then the party announced that Atiku and other national leaders of the party were expected to arrive in Sokoto at 9am through the Sultan Abubakar III International Airport. The announcement cleared the air over the controversy which came with conflicting reports on where the event would be held. Our correspondents report that supporters of the ADC turned Atiku’s arrival into a carnival as they intensified their call for a change of government, repeatedly chanting “Tinubu Must Go”. The slogan rang out at the Sultan Abubakar III International Airport, Sokoto, where party supporters gathered to welcome Atiku and his entourage, with members of the Tinubu Must Go Movement leading the chant. Atiku and his entourage arrived in Sokoto at about 1 pm but did not reach the ADC State Secretariat, the venue of the campaign rally, until around 4:30 pm, following the large crowd that turned out to welcome them. The journey from the airport to the city centre would ordinarily take no more than 15 minutes. The triple-lane airport road was filled with ADC supporters waving party flags and displaying campaign posters and banners of the party’s candidates. Many sang, danced and celebrated along the route. The campaign venue was also filled to capacity, with some supporters climbing onto the roof of the party’s four-storey secretariat. item.title: Weak labour movement ‘ll hurt all, not just workers – NLC
item.description: By Victor Ahiuma-Young The consequences of a weakened labour movement could extend far beyond factories, government offices and other workplaces, leaving millions of Nigerians without a strong collective voice to challenge policies affecting their economic survival, rights and welfare. Read Also: N70,000 Transport Allowance Saga: ‘You can’t lead TUC from abroad,’ Ajaero tells Osifo For the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC), the strength of organised labour is not just a trade union concern but a matter that directly affects the wellbeing of the entire country. Beyond its traditional responsibility of negotiating wages and protecting workers’ interests, Labour movement has historically served as an important platform for defending ordinary Nigerians, challenging unpopular government policies and protecting the civic space. Its weakening, therefore, could have consequences for people who are not necessarily members of any trade union but whose livelihoods are affected by government decisions. This was the concern expressed by the President of the NLC, Joe Ajaero, who warned that Nigerians would become victims if the labour movement collapsed. “If the labour movement collapses today, all of us will become victims,” Ajaero declared in Lagos, while speaking at the 2026 Annual Conference of the Labour Writers Association of Nigeria (LAWAN), themed: Workers at the Centre of Nigeria’s Political Transition: Defending Rights, Advancing Welfare and Building Economic Justice. His warning was particularly directed at Nigerians who appear to regard the struggles of organised labour as the exclusive responsibility of workers and trade union leaders, even when the issues being contested affect their daily lives. According to him, the labour movement remains one of the important voices defending the interests of ordinary Nigerians, adding that its collapse would leave workers and other vulnerable groups with fewer platforms through which to express their grievances. He said: “If that voice becomes weak, workers and other vulnerable groups will have fewer platforms through which to express their grievances.” For Ajaero, the danger is that a weakened labour movement would not only affect the ability of workers to negotiate better conditions of service but could also reduce the capacity of ordinary citizens to collectively challenge economic policies that worsen their living conditions. He questioned the attitude of Nigerians who complain about the rising cost of living but expect the NLC to take responsibility for confronting every challenge without corresponding public support. “It is not enough to complain about the cost of fuel, transportation, food or other necessities and then ask where the NLC is,” he said. “The labour movement cannot solve every problem without the participation and support of the people.” The NLC president argued that the struggle for affordable living conditions should not be left to organised labour alone because the consequences of economic

item.title: Amidst heatwave, electricity supply shortage bites harder
item.description: From Abdullateef Aliyu, Mohammed Musbau and Dotun Omisakin, Lagos; Yusuf Akogu and Idris Bature (Abuja); Hamisu Kabir Matazu, Maiduguri; Ahmad Datti, Kano and Promise Adagba The worsening electricity supply situation across several parts of the country has heightened the hardship residents face amid the recent heatwave, Daily Trust reports. From Lagos to Abuja, Kano, Maiduguri, Ondo State, Kwara, and other states, residents have lamented declining electricity supply, with some reporting outages lasting days or weeks. The situation has forced many households to adopt uncomfortable and, in some cases, risky measures to survive the heat, while businesses dependent on electricity are counting their losses. In Lagos, the frustration over persistent blackouts recently spilled onto the streets as residents of Lagos Island staged a protest, demanding an immediate restoration of electricity to their communities. The demonstration, which took place on Tuesday, involved mainly women from Lewis, Okesuna, Beecroft, Simpson and Sandgrouse streets, who expressed anger over prolonged power outages and the discomfort caused by rising temperatures. They called on the electricity distribution company to address their plight. The residents said the absence of electricity had compounded the discomfort caused by intense heat, leaving households struggling to sleep, preserve food and carry out daily activities. The situation has been attributed in some areas to constraints in power generation and reduced electricity allocation from the national grid. In August, Eko Electricity Distribution Company (EKEDC) reportedly said its allocation had fallen from 486 megawatts to 347 megawatts, forcing it to adjust electricity supply to some feeders. The latest demonstration also followed a warning by the Lagos State Government about the possibility of extreme heat as the dry season approaches and the El Niño climate pattern strengthens. Following the El Nino weather pattern, it has been projected that Nigeria could record an additional 31,400 heat-related deaths between September 2026 and February 2027. The projection by the Climate Impact Lab places Nigeria among the countries expected to suffer the highest number of additional heat-related deaths globally during the six-month period of El Niño, with nearly half of the 66,800 deaths projected across the Sahel region expected to occur in the country. However, the combination of high temperatures and unreliable electricity has heightened residents’ concerns, especially over their ability to keep homes comfortable and businesses operating. The situation is no different on Lagos Mainland, where residents have been without electricity supply for the past few days. The Ikeja Electricity Distribution Company, which serves the Lagos Mainland and some parts of Ogun State, has been sending apologies to the residents over the blackout. item.title: Destruction of campaign posters, billboards: Police read riot act to politicians, thugs, miscreants
item.description: *IGP orders Police Commissioners to arrest, prosecute offenders *Avert Obi, Kwankwaso /APC supporters clash in Calabar By Kingsley Omonobi & Ike Uchechukwu ABUJA — Force headquarters yesterday warned politicians, thugs, miscreants and other persons with affiliations to members of the political class responsible for destruction of campaign posters, billboards and banners belonging to candidates and parties to desist or face prosecution. The warning came against the backdrop of persistent complaints by political parties and their candidates about how thugs allegedly sponsored by their opponents had continuously destroyed their campaign materials, making it impossible to market themselves to the electorate. This came on a day Police and other security operatives prevented a possible violent clash in Calabar, Cross River State,between hundreds of supporters of Peter Obi and Rabiu Kwankwaso and a large group of All Progressives Congress, APC, supporters on campaign walk. Giving the warning yesterday, Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Aniete Iniedu, said in a statement that those who chose to break the law will face the full consequences of their actions. The statement read: “The Nigeria Police Force has observed with serious concern the growing incidents of deliberate tearing, defacement and destruction of political campaign posters, banners and billboards belonging to candidates and political parties across the country ahead of the 2027 general elections. “The Force strongly condemns this act of political intolerance and warns political thugs, hoodlums and other mischief-makers involved to desist immediately. “For the avoidance of doubt, destroying, defacing or unlawfully removing another candidate’s campaign posters and billboards may constitute malicious damage, which is a criminal offence under applicable criminal laws (Section 451 of the Criminal Code Act and Section 326 of the Penal Code Law which defines the offence of mischief). ‘Political differences or loyalty to a particular party do not give anyone the right to destroy another candidate’s property or infringe on their right to campaign freely. “The Force reiterates that all political parties and candidates, irrespective of their affiliation or status, are entitled to equal protection under the law. “No individual or group has the right to determine whose campaign materials should be displayed or destroyed. item.title: Senate proposes six-month jail term for hospitals denying emergency care
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Senate has passed for second reading a bill seeking to make it compulsory for public and private hospitals across Nigeria to provide emergency medical treatment, prescribing up to six months’ imprisonment for facilities and individuals who violate its provisions. The proposed legislation also prescribes a fine of up to ₦300,000, imprisonment for six months, or both, for anyone convicted of denying emergency medical treatment. The bill, sponsored by Senator Abdulaziz Musa Yar’Adua (APC, Katsina Central), seeks to amend the National Health Act, 2014, to establish mandatory emergency medical treatment standards and referral protocols in healthcare facilities. Titled, “A Bill for an Act to Amend the National Health Act, 2014 to Provide for Emergency Medical Treatment Standards and Referral Protocols in Healthcare Facilities; and for Related Matters, 2026” (SB. 759), it was referred to the Senate Committee on Health (Secondary and Tertiary) for further legislative action, with a directive to report back in four weeks. Under the proposed amendment, no healthcare provider, health worker or medical establishment would be allowed to deny anyone emergency medical treatment for any reason. It also requires healthcare professionals to commence life-saving interventions, including cardiopulmonary resuscitation, airway management and bleeding control, immediately after identifying a life-threatening condition. The bill proposes that hospitals conduct triage and initial assessments within 15 minutes of a patient’s arrival, while basic stabilisation measures, including oxygen administration, intravenous fluids, pain management and initial diagnostic procedures, must begin within 30 minutes. For patients requiring admission, hospital beds are to be assigned within two hours, subject to availability. Where beds are unavailable, healthcare facilities would be required to commence immediate stabilisation and arrange the patient’s transfer to another hospital. The proposed legislation further requires hospitals to initiate referral arrangements within two hours and complete the transfer process within three hours of a patient’s arrival, except where circumstances beyond their control prevent compliance. It also mandates hospitals to dispatch an ambulance or arrange alternative transportation within 30 minutes of communicating a referral decision. Beyond emergency response timelines, the bill seeks to introduce mandatory emergency care training and certification for healthcare workers, with recertification intervals not exceeding 18 months. It also mandates the Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria and the Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria to jointly develop a standardised national emergency care curriculum. However, healthcare practitioners would be protected from penalties where resource constraints prevent compliance, provided the challenges are properly documented and prescribed referral procedures are followed. item.title: Duty & Allegiance: Gowon’s memoirs, an exercise in self-justification! By Olu Fasan
item.description: In the Acknowledgements section of his recently published memoirs My Life of Duty & Allegiance, General Yakubu Gowon, a former military head of state, writes: “Let me begin by saying that I was not anxious to document my memoirs, but the calls for me to do so kept coming.” Well, I am one of those who kept urging General Gowon to write his memoirs. I did so in three interventions in this column, the last of which, in March last year, was daringly titled “A plea to General Gowon: Sir, write your memoir before you die!” (Vanguard, March 13, 2025). So, when Gowon published his memoirs in May this year, I did not hesitate to spend £29.98 (about N54,000) to buy a copy from Amazon. I read the 760-page book with great interest! First, congratulations are in order! General Gowon truly deserves commendation for writing such a historically significant book. His was the last voice everyone wanted to hear on the most epochal events in the annals of this country: the 1966 coups and civil war, during which he was head of state. Gowon addresses those thorny issues in the memoirs, a masterpiece. The book starts with General Gowon’s removal from power in July 1975. Chapter 1, titled “Our Boys Are Up To Something”, deals with the coup that toppled him while he was attending a summit of the then Organisation of African Union, OAU, in Kampala, Uganda. This is instructive because the memoirs, divided into 36 chapters, are almost entirely Gowon’s ripostes to various allegations and criticisms against him. He leaves virtually no allegation or criticism unaddressed. And on each, he admits no wrong, no fault, no error! It was entirely an exercise in self-justification, without a single mea culpa! It is impossible to discuss Gowon’s comprehensive memoirs in one column, and I won’t do so here. In other columns, I would address the quality of governance and the public service ethos under General Gowon’s regime, as well as the 1966 coups and the civil war. In the present intervention, however, my focus is on what I regard as the memoirs’ general flaws, one being its somewhat weak evidential base. Reading the book, it struck me that, in some places, much of what General Gowon says is based on conjectures, insinuations and assertions. Of course, unlike an autobiography, which requires research, dates and facts, a memoir is usually based on memory and subjective interpretation. Nevertheless, the recounting of significant events in Nigeria’s past by one of its key dramatis personae should not be devoid of historical accuracy. To be fair, General Gowon explains the paucity of evidence, saying: “I want to emphasise that I am telling my story without access to my crucial personal records, since many important documents taken from my desk after my removal in July 1975 were discarded by those who succeeded me.” Of course, in doing so, those people denude Nigeria’s historical narrative of richness. The documents that survived, Gowon says, “were destroyed by two serial fire incidents.”

item.title: 2027: Atiku Vows To Tackle Insecurity At Sokoto Campaign Flag-Off, Says Nothing Will Stop ADC
item.description: Presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, has reaffirmed his commitment to tackling insecurity, declaring that alleged attempts to frustrate his party’s campaign will not stop its activities ahead of the 2027 general election. “I enumerated some of the promises I made to Nigerians. One of the promises is to make sure that security is restored in every part of this country.” ﻿ Atiku spoke on Wednesday at the flag-off of his presidential campaign in Sokoto, where he urged Nigerians to support the ADC and vote for the party in the forthcoming election. His declaration came a day after he accused the Sokoto State Government and security operatives of plotting to disrupt the campaign rally, alleging that the Department of State Services (DSS) was recruiting protesters to cause disturbances and create a situation that could be used to impose a curfew. Crowd at the flag off of Atiku Abubakar campaign in Sokoto on Wednesday, November 4, 2026. At a news conference in Abuja on Tuesday, the former Vice President also accused the state government of denying the ADC access to public facilities and logistical support for the rally. He described the alleged restrictions as deliberate attempts to deny the opposition party a level playing field. The DSS subsequently ordered an investigation into Atiku’s allegation, saying the directive was issued by its Director-General despite the Service describing the claim as inconsistent with its operations. In its response, the agency said its operatives had provided security protection to political actors across party lines. It cited an incident involving the ADC governorship candidate in Sokoto, Mannir Daniya, whom its personnel reportedly evacuated to safety after he was attacked on October 31. Despite the controversy, Atiku proceeded with the campaign flag-off, saying no attempt to frustrate the party would deter it from addressing the people of Sokoto. Crowd at the flag off of Atiku Abubakar campaign in Sokoto on Wednesday, November 4, 2026. He explained that the state was deliberately chosen for the campaign launch because of its historical significance and reputation for peace. The ADC candidate recalled the promises he made during his previous campaign, saying he had returned to reaffirm his commitment to those pledges, particularly his promise to tackle insecurity if elected president. He also called on Nigerians to turn out in large numbers on election day and vote for the ADC, expressing confidence in the party’s political mission. The rally marks the formal commencement of Atiku’s presidential campaign activities in Sokoto ahead of the 2027 general election. item.title: VIDEO: Tinubu, Atiku Are Old, They Should Allow Younger Ones To Lead – Oyinlola
item.description: Former Osun State Governor Olagunsoye Oyinlola has said President Bola Tinubu and former Vice President Atiku Abubakar should retire from active politics and allow younger Nigerians to take over the country’s leadership. Oyinlola, a member of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), said he supports Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde, who is seeking the presidency on the platform of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), for the 2027 election. Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Wednesday, the former governor argued that age should be a consideration in determining who seeks public office. “When I was in Osun, I made a declaration based on my experience in office that anybody above 50 should not aspire to be governor of a state,” Oyinlola said. He maintained that Tinubu and Atiku should step aside to give younger elements an opportunity to lead Nigeria. ﻿ The post VIDEO: Tinubu, Atiku Are Old, They Should Allow Younger Ones To Lead – Oyinlola appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Tinubu Returns To Abuja After Umrah In Saudi Arabia
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has returned to Abuja after performing the Umrah pilgrimage in Saudi Arabia. The President’s aircraft landed at the Presidential Wing of the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport at 8:53 p.m. on Wednesday. He was received on arrival by the Chief of Staff, Femi Gbajabiamila; the Minister of Education, Tunji Alausa; the Minister of State for Defence; the Inspector-General of Police and other government officials. ﻿ Tinubu departed King Abdulaziz International Airport, Jeddah, at 5:13 p.m. Saudi time after completing the lesser Hajj in Makkah. Before his departure, the President held a brief meeting with the Deputy Governor of Makkah Region, Prince Saud bin Mishal bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, at the Royal Guest Palace within the airport. During the visit, Tinubu led members of the Nigerian delegation in performing the Umrah rites, including the circumambulation of the Holy Ka’abah. He was also granted the privilege of entering the Holy Ka’abah on Sunday, where he and members of his delegation performed two raka’at prayers. According to a statement by his spokesperson, Bayo Onanuga, the President offered prayers for Nigeria’s peace, security, unity and prosperity, as well as divine guidance and wisdom for the country’s leaders. His entourage included the National Security Adviser, Nuhu Ribadu, and the governors of Sokoto, Jigawa, Kaduna, Borno and Yobe States, among others.
